prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: checked baggage from bag-drop/transfer induction through screening, sorting, make-up to outbound load handoff. Elements: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit (sends Oversize Exception Ticket to Image Resolution Desk); Bag Tag Printer (unique-ID tag; Calibration Witness Tag used by Maintenance Technician); Transfer Bag Feeder (sends Late Transfer Bag Card to Bag Reconciliation Station); Induction Tray Conveyor (metering; carries only bags with readable ID and valid route into screening); Baggage Control System, alias Velvet (authoritative record: identity, flight, screening disposition, handling status; routing, sort plan; exceptions to Secondary Inspection Chute; receives Flight Cutoff Advisory; records alarms, dispositions/checks for traceability; authorizes rejoin); Concourse Zone Controller, alias Mosslight (induction permissive; Recovery Route Card; lane assignment; no screening bypass); Flight Data Gateway, alias Lantern (flight/destination data; sends Flight Cutoff Advisory; confirms operating departure); Primary Crossbelt Sorter, alias Juniper (cleared bags to make-up, diverts unresolved; Chute Occupancy Note to Supervisor); North Gate Scanner, alias Kestrel; South Gate Scanner (Manual Rescan Receipt to Desk); both must report healthy before results used; Image Resolution Desk (reviews images, records disposition before continuation); Secondary Inspection Chute (kept clear of unrelated bags); Bag Reconciliation Station (Bag Match Query); East/West Make-Up Conveyors (guards closed); Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit, alias Orchard (receives Carousel Release Slip; releases only with valid disposition and destination); Outbound Load Control Desk. Actors: Baggage Operations Supervisor, alias Tern (approvals, holds, stop induction; ensures holds/exceptions have owner before continuation); Explosives Response Team, alias Pebble (Custody Seal Log; assesses referred events, communicates disposition); Security Duty Manager (uses seal log, escalates discrepancies; access control); Maintenance Technician (isolates energy; reports faults affecting identity/screening/access before return to service); Airline Ramp Coordinator (sends Carousel Release Slip). States: clear, exception, awaiting review, hold, safe state. Requirements: hold missing/conflicting/oversized/mismatched or unresolved-screening bags in controlled hold area; stop gives safe state without disabling unrelated routes; recovery starts with inspection and bag accounting; route/flight change needs approval; restart needs personnel clear, guards restored, alarms understood, route available; controlled custody from screening release to authorized loading handoff;

New part:
S218: The Bag Reconciliation Station compares scanned bag identities against the expected flight population and flags missing or duplicate records for resolution.
S219: The Airline Ramp Coordinator uses the Bag Match Query to review unresolved bag-to-flight mismatches before loading authorization is granted.
S220: The East Make-Up Conveyor moves reconciled bags toward the correct flight position without bypassing required identity checks.
S221: The West Make-Up Conveyor remains subject to the same controlled access and reconciliation rules as other make-up equipment.
S222: The Transfer Bag Feeder accepts transfer bags only when their identity and intended onward flight can be verified.
S223: The Outbound Load Control Desk confirms that the flight assignment, reconciled bag count, and operational status are consistent before accepting the loading record.
S224: Before aircraft loading, the Airline Ramp Coordinator verifies that the bag identity is readable, the flight assignment is current, and the security disposition permits loading.
S225: The physical bags presented for loading must agree with the reconciled records, and every unexplained count or identity difference blocks acceptance.
S226: A bag is ready for departure only after screening release, custody continuity, final reconciliation, and loading checks are all complete and recorded.
S227: Operational monitoring provides a continuous view of baggage throughput, equipment availability, queue growth, screening status, and reconciliation exceptions.
S228: The Baggage Control System records bag events and reports missing, duplicate, or delayed event sequences for operational review.
S229: The Concourse Zone Controller reports equipment state changes and alarm conditions to the operations monitoring function.
S230: The Induction Tray Conveyor is monitored for stops, accumulation, and sustained operation below its approved rate.
S231: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter is monitored for availability, recirculation, fault frequency, and output rate against the approved operating plan.
S232: North Gate Scanner performance is assessed using availability, image capture quality, alarm frequency, and screening completion records.
S233: South Gate Scanner performance is assessed using the same approved service measures and screening completion criteria.
S234: The Image Resolution Desk reports unresolved images, review backlog, and processing time against the locally approved service target.
S235: The Bag Reconciliation Station reports unmatched records and count differences, which remain subject to resolution before acceptance.
S236: The Flight Data Gateway is monitored for message timeliness, completeness, and interface errors affecting flight assignment data.
S237: The Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit is monitored for service availability, transaction completion, and accumulation at its entry point.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
